description: DHS TRIP is the designated channel for travellers who experience repeated secondary screening, boarding denials, unexplained delays or unusual questioning.
energy_note: There is a form. That is the remedy.

description: Many frequent fliers report their TRIP appeals have not helped. DHS OIG reporting has noted mismatches affecting low-risk travellers with redress mechanisms not fully mitigating false positives.
energy_note: Filed, acknowledged, and screened again next month.

aspect: You cannot find out whether you are listed
description: There is no route to confirm listing or learn the reason. Litigation has been the only mechanism - CAIR's Baby Doe v. Piehota was brought by 19 plaintiffs to find out why they were on the list at all.
energy_note: Suing to be told whether you are on a list.

aspect: So you build your life around the assumption
description: Arrive four hours early. Never book a tight connection. Never check a bag you need. Never travel the day before something that matters. The adaptation is permanent and costs money on every trip.
money_note: Annual cost of defensive travel planning.
energy_note: Planning every journey around a search.

aspect: EXAMPLE - suing in order to be told
description: There is no route to confirm whether you are listed or why. Litigation has been the only mechanism: CAIR's Baby Doe v. Piehota was brought by 19 plaintiffs against DHS, the FBI, TSA and the Terrorist Screening Center simply to find out why they were on the watchlist.
energy_note: Nineteen people, in federal court, asking why.
